results.title: AI can spark creativity — if we ask it how, not what, to think - Nature
results.content: # AI can spark creativity — if we ask it how, not what, to think. Studies aiming to maximize human creativity demonstrate that people work best when buoyed up by others who show them new ways to innovate. However, in practice, the opposite is often true — bots flatten creativity. Can AI be truly creative? As a researcher who has spent 30 years studying human creativity, I think I know why. When a scientist feeds a data set into a bot and says “give me hypotheses to test”, they are asking the bot to be the creator, not a creative partner. Instead, researchers should learn how to use bots to boost their creativity. I’ve been working with a test of rapid creative thinking called the divergent association task (DAT), which I think points to a way forwards.
